problem: The integral condition is garbled: it reads '0−BBESD(ω)dω = η(2πE)', which a student cannot parse as a definite integral from −B to B. The relation itself is correct, but the broken notation hides the limits and the meaning of the factor 2πE.
fix: Write it cleanly: ∫<sub>−B</sub><sup>B</sup> ESD(ω) dω = η(2πE), where η is the fraction of total energy (0 < η < 1) and E is the total energy in J. Equivalently (1/2π)∫<sub>−B</sub><sup>B</sup> ESD(ω) dω = ηE.

problem: The caption and aria text say the scaled two-sided area is the energy 1/6 J, but the plotted ω axis runs only from 0 to 10 rad/s. The area under the visible one-sided curve is half of that, 1/12 J, so the figure and its caption disagree, and this is exactly the one-sided/two-sided confusion warned about in exam trap 3.
fix: State in the caption that only ω ≥ 0 is displayed, that the shown half contributes 1/12 J, and that the full two-sided integral (1/2π)∫<sub>−∞</sub><sup>∞</sup>|X(ω)|²dω equals 1/6 J. Also label the y axis with units: 'ESD (J per rad/s)'.

problem: The text is corrupted: 'for t0∞ e^{−6t}dt' loses the case t < 0 and the lower limit of the integral, so the step cannot be read as written.
fix: For t ≥ 0, |x(t)|² = e^{−6t}; for t < 0, x(t) = 0. So E = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>∞</sup> e^{−6t} dt.
